Platform owners, not robot makers, are capturing the value
  • NVIDIA, Qualcomm and Arm bundle silicon, software and a developer funnel.
  • 73.6% of Unitree's humanoid revenue came from research and education (first nine months of 2025).

BIt impacts the language of business decision-making

DecisionThe choiceWhat it shapes
ChipNVIDIA, Qualcomm, or a cheaper niche chipUnit cost, power, switching cost
ModelSmall open model on the device, or a cloud APIQuality, running cost per use
Where it runsEdge, cloud, or hybridSpeed, privacy, uptime
2
Small open models now run on the device
  • Gemma 4: open models for on-device agents (April 2026, Apache 2.0).
  • NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge: a 4B-parameter model that runs on the robot.

CThere is room for research and innovation

  • Swarms: drone mesh networks that keep working when masts fail (Fraunhofer IIS, research).
  • Photonic chips: neural networks computed with light on a silicon chip (Heidelberg University, 2026).
  • Bigger models on small devices: quantization made Meta's Llama 56% smaller (vendor claim); 2026 research also compresses working memory.
3
Automotive is the cash cow today
  • Qualcomm automotive: $1.59B in the June 2026 quarter, up 61%.
  • Mobileye EyeQ: in more than 250M vehicles as of July 2026.

Four sections take us from what Edge AI is to who captures the value

Click a section to jump to it. Press I on any slide to return here.

Edge AI runs the model on the device itself, not in a distant data center

Where "the edge" is

CarDriver assistance and self-driving
RobotHumanoids, factory arms, warehouse robots
CameraInspection lines, traffic signals, smart cameras
PhoneAssistants that work without a connection
Factory gatewayA local AI box next to the machines

One example: the autonomous vehicle

  • It must see and decide on board: it can't wait for a network.
  • The cameras, the chip and the model all travel with the car.
  • Waymo runs 3,000+ robotaxis that drive on board and ask for remote help in edge cases.
  • The cloud still trains the models and ships fleet-wide updates.
Source: Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026); TechCrunch (Mar 27, 2026) for the Waymo fleet: 3,067 robotaxis in a December 2025 filing with the US road-safety regulator; Waymo blog (Dec 23, 2025) for remote confirmation checks.

While Edge AI performs better on latency, privacy and reliability, it falls behind on quality

For discussion, not exhaustive
DriverWhy it mattersConcrete example
Edge AI winsLatency / real-time controlRobots and cars must act in milliseconds.Gemini Robotics On-Device runs its control model "directly on the robot" (Google DeepMind).
Privacy / sovereigntySome data can't leave the site or the country.Qualcomm Dragonwing AI On-Prem Appliance: sovereign, fully offline inference and training.
Reliability / offlineFactories, vehicles and robots can't depend on a network.Mobileye EyeQ does perception on board in 250M+ vehicles (as of July 2026).
Cloud winsQualityBigger models still perform better, so hybrid is the default.DeepMind's own chart: on-device model about 0.68 vs about 0.8 for the flagship when adapting to new tasks (June 2025 version). Its planning model (ER 2) is served from the cloud while control runs locally.
Rule of thumb: put the reflexes on the device and keep the hard planning, training and updates in the cloud.
Source: Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026), "Why edge vs. cloud", citing Google DeepMind, Qualcomm press release, Mobileye 10-Q and Ynetnews. The 0.68 vs 0.8 scores are DeepMind's fast-adaptation test for Gemini Robotics On-Device v1 (June 2025); no comparable figure was found for On-Device 2 (July 2026).

Your call: where should hospital imaging triage run?

Use case 1 of 4 · illustrative scenario
A hospital wants AI to flag urgent scans so radiologists read them first.
Scans are sensitive patient data. Minutes matter, not milliseconds. Hard cases need the best model available.
Vote first: click a card to mark the room's pick.
Privacy / sovereignty → edgePatient scans get a first pass on site, so raw data stays in the hospital.
Reliability → edgeTriage keeps working if the link drops. Medical-grade edge platforms exist (IGX Thor).
Quality gap → cloudAmbiguous cases escalate to larger models and specialists; training stays central.
Source: illustrative scenario and suggested answer by the presenter, using the drivers on slide 6. IGX Thor medical imaging platforms: ADLINK, via Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026).

Your call: where should a factory defect-inspection camera run?

Use case 2 of 4 · illustrative scenario
A camera checks every part on a fast production line and rejects defects.
The line must not stop if the network does. The images show proprietary products.
Vote first: click a card to mark the room's pick.
Latency → edgeThe reject decision must land in milliseconds, before the part moves on.
Reliability → edgeA network outage can't be allowed to stop production.
Privacy → edgeProduct images stay in the plant. The cloud only retrains and updates the model.
Source: illustrative scenario and suggested answer by the presenter, using the drivers on slide 6. Industrial vendors building on Jetson Thor (FANUC, Hitachi, Techman): NVIDIA, via Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026).

Your call: where should a customer-service chatbot run?

Use case 3 of 4 · illustrative scenario
A retailer wants a chatbot that answers order and returns questions on its website.
Users are already online. Answers need live order data and the best language quality.
Vote first: click a card to mark the room's pick.
Latency → no edge caseNothing physical to control; a one-second reply is fine.
Reliability → no edge caseThe customer is on the website, so the connection already exists.
Quality gap → cloudThe largest models answer best and update instantly. Strict privacy rules could change this.
Source: illustrative scenario and suggested answer by the presenter, using the drivers on slide 6 (Edge AI Navigation Map, Oct 2026, "Why edge vs. cloud").

Your call: where should a crop-spraying drone's AI run?

Use case 4 of 4 · illustrative scenario
A drone sprays fields far from reliable coverage.
It must hold its path and avoid obstacles in real time. One pilot supervises several drones.
Vote first: click a card to mark the room's pick.
Latency → edgeFlight control and obstacle avoidance can't wait for a round trip.
Reliability → edgeThe field has no dependable link, so the drone decides on board.
Real example: HylioIn 2024 the FAA let one pilot fly 3 Hylio spray drones: up to 150 acres per hour (vendor claim). Coordination is local ground control, not cloud.
Source: illustrative scenario and suggested answer by the presenter, using the drivers on slide 6. Hylio: FAA exemption of Feb 27, 2024 and AgWeb, via Edge AI Infrastructure for Civilian Swarms (Oct 2026).

Edge AI is enabling decentralized swarms for complex use cases

PatternHow it worksCivilian example
Truly decentralized: no central controller
Fully decentralized peer-to-peerEach agent broadcasts its state and decides locally; no base station.C-V2X car-to-car safety messages; Fraunhofer IIS drone mesh (research).
On-device agent meshSmall models on phones, PCs or gateways negotiate tasks peer-to-peer.No verified production deployment (research only).
Hybrid: local autonomy, with help from the center
Hybrid with remote assistVehicles drive locally; edge cases escalate to remote humans or cloud models.Waymo remote confirmation; Gemini Robotics ER 2.
Centrally coordinated: a planner still runs the show
Central choreographyA ground computer scripts every trajectory; drones just execute.EHang Egret: 22,580-drone show "from a single computer".
One operator, many vehiclesOne certified human supervises several semi-autonomous vehicles.Hylio: 3 crop-spraying drones per pilot.
On-site fleet managerA local manager assigns missions; robots handle perception and motion on board.Warehouse robots (idealworks AnyFleet, Destro MothershipOS).

NVIDIA's strategy is to sell the Edge AI brain together with the software that locks customers in

NVIDIA deep dive
ProductWhat it isKey facts

Side note: the lock-in

  • Thor runs inside NVIDIA's software ecosystem: Isaac GR00T and Cosmos.
  • CUDA, TensorRT and Isaac make switching chips costly.

How NVIDIA makes money here

  • Hardware margin on modules and developer kits ($3,499 kit).
  • Partners (Advantech, ADLINK) build the systems.
  • Three-computer pitch: train, simulate, deploy. Edge customers also buy data center.

Its own AI chip designs for small devices: Ethos NPUs

  • Ethos-U: AI accelerator designs for low-power chips.

Four open questions will decide how far Edge AI spreads beyond cars

What efficiency gains are needed to deploy small models at scale outside automotive?
  • A flagship robot computer draws 40–130 W and costs $3,499 as a kit.
  • DeepMind's first on-device robot model trailed its flagship: about 0.68 vs 0.8 (June 2025).
  • 73.6% of Unitree's humanoid revenue came from research and education.
Is memory a hidden bottleneck?
  • Analysts tie NVIDIA's smaller Thor modules to locking down memory supply.
  • Memory costs are squeezing Qualcomm's handset margins.
  • A 4B-class phone model peaks above 3 GB of RAM on CPU.
Will NVIDIA's platform also win at the edge?
  • For: a full stack from simulation to on-robot model to safety system.
  • Against: trade press reads Qualcomm's robotics chip as aimed at Jetson; Tesla and Chinese automakers build their own chips.
  • Edge is under 8% of NVIDIA's revenue: $7.2B vs $89.0B.
Will robot makers capture a higher share of the value vs platform owners?
  • Today most don't: robot makers depend on Thor or Dragonwing, which depend on Arm.
  • Unitree is the exception: profitable in 2025 on about RMB 1.7B of revenue.
  • Vertical integrators such as Tesla keep the chip margin in-house.
Source: Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026), including its value-chain section, citing NVIDIA, ServeTheHome, Google DeepMind, The Robot Report, Jon Peddie Research (July 20, 2026), the Qualcomm FQ3 2026 call and NVIDIA's Q2 FY27 release; memory figures from slide 20 (Google LiteRT-LM and Meta model card); in-house chips from slide 13.

Edge AI is already a real business, and anyone building a product will face its choices

Back-up

It is already here

250M+
vehicles built with Mobileye EyeQ chips, as of July 2026
Ynetnews (secondary); 248M in Mobileye's Q1 10-Q
+61%
Qualcomm automotive revenue, to $1.59B in the June 2026 quarter
23rd straight double-digit quarter (Zacks)
  • Edge AI is the link between AI models and real-world deployment.
  • The revenue is real today in cars and connected devices.
  • Humanoid robots are still mostly bought by research labs and schools.

If you build a prototype or a start-up, you decide

DecisionThe choiceWhat it shapes
ChipNVIDIA, Qualcomm, or a cheaper niche chipUnit cost, power, switching cost
ModelSmall open model on the device, or a cloud APIQuality, running cost per use
Where it runsEdge, cloud, or hybridSpeed, privacy, uptime
These three choices set your cost, your margin and your lock-in.

Three trends decide who makes money in edge AI

Back-up
1
Small open models now run on the device
  • Gemma 4: open models for on-device agents (April 2026, Apache 2.0).
  • NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge: a 4B-parameter model that runs on the robot.
So what: inference cost moves to the customer's hardware; the model becomes a feature of the device.
2
Platform owners, not robot makers, capture the value
  • NVIDIA, Qualcomm and Arm bundle silicon, software and a developer funnel.
  • Unitree closed Sept 9 about 39% below its debut close.
  • 73.6% of its humanoid revenue came from research and education (first nine months of 2025).
So what: own the ecosystem the robots are built on, not the robot.
3
Automotive is the cash cow today
  • Qualcomm automotive: $1.59B in the June 2026 quarter, up 61%.
  • Mobileye EyeQ: in more than 250M vehicles as of July 2026.
So what: cars are the proven, high-volume source of edge AI revenue.
Source: Edge AI Navigation Map (Oct 2026), citing Google Developers Blog, NVIDIA blog, The Robot Report (Unitree), TelecomLead and Zacks (Qualcomm FQ3 2026), Ynetnews and Mobileye 10-Q.

Most "swarms" still have a central brain; only two of six patterns are truly decentralized

Back-up
PatternHow it worksCivilian example
Truly decentralized: no central controller
Fully decentralized peer-to-peerEach agent broadcasts its state and decides locally; no base station.C-V2X car-to-car safety messages; Fraunhofer IIS drone mesh (research).
On-device agent meshSmall models on phones, PCs or gateways negotiate tasks peer-to-peer.No verified production deployment (research only).
Centrally coordinated: a planner still runs the show
Central choreographyA ground computer scripts every trajectory; drones just execute.EHang Egret: 22,580-drone show "from a single computer".
One operator, many vehiclesOne certified human supervises several semi-autonomous vehicles.Hylio: 3 crop-spraying drones per pilot.
On-site fleet managerA local manager assigns missions; robots handle perception and motion on board.Warehouse robots (idealworks AnyFleet, Destro MothershipOS).
Hybrid with remote assistVehicles drive locally; edge cases escalate to remote humans or cloud models.Waymo remote confirmation; Gemini Robotics ER 2.
Source: Edge AI Infrastructure for Civilian Swarms (Oct 2026), Phase 3 architecture patterns, citing Qualcomm, Fraunhofer IIS, DroneXL (EHang), AgWeb (Hylio), idealworks, Destro AI, TechCrunch (Waymo) and Google DeepMind.

Swarms don't need a cloud LLM to react, but a central planner still wins on quality and control

Back-up
FactorNo cloud LLM neededCloud / central planner still wins
LatencyCollision avoidance and car-to-car warnings need sub-second response.Multi-minute task plans tolerate a cloud round trip.
Connectivity lossDisaster zones with damaged masts; offline industrial sites.When the network is up and exceptions are rare.
ScaleLocal broadcast scales with no server bottleneck.One computer already flies 22,580 drones.
Planning qualityGood enough for reactive behaviour.Flagship models still beat on-device versions.
Updates / governance—Training, fleet-wide updates and audit trails stay central.

When the center fails: Waymo, San Francisco

Blackout of Dec 20, 2025
  • Cars crossed 7,000+ dark signals on their own.
  • A spike in remote-confirmation requests then stalled vehicles at intersections.
  • Cell networks were down too.
  • Waymo paused service and began rolling out a fleet-wide update.
Local autonomy worked. The central dependency was the weak point.
Source: Edge AI Infrastructure for Civilian Swarms (Oct 2026), "When swarms need no cloud LLM", citing Fraunhofer IIS, Google DeepMind, DroneXL (EHang), TechCrunch (Dec 21, 2025) and Axios (Dec 22, 2025) on the Waymo blackout.

Only car-to-car safety messaging runs as a true peer-to-peer swarm in production today

Back-up
Production · peer-to-peer

C-V2X sidelink

  • Cars broadcast safety messages directly to each other.
  • Works with "no infrastructure and SIM required".
  • Deployed in China and in US state projects such as Virginia (vendor claim, Qualcomm).
Pilot

Wildfire response

  • Dryad Networks: sensor mesh in production; suppression drones due for pilots in 2027 (vendor claim).
  • Seneca: five-drone strike team; CAL FIRE field test in July 2026.
  • Fire service view: "still work to do" before operational use.
Research

Drone mesh networks

  • Fraunhofer IIS: decentralized mesh radio for civilian drone swarms.
  • Built for disaster zones where masts fail.
  • Initial findings published June 2026; simulation and lab stage.
Centrally coordinated

Light shows & warehouses

  • EHang: 22,580 drones flown "from a single computer".
  • Warehouse fleets: a central fleet manager assigns every mission.
  • Large scale, in production, but not a self-organizing swarm.
Source: Edge AI Infrastructure for Civilian Swarms (Oct 2026), Phase 4 deployments, citing Qualcomm C-V2X primer, sUAS News (Dryad), The Robot Report and DroneXL (Seneca), Lancashire Fire and Rescue Service, Fraunhofer IIS (June 2026), DroneXL (EHang) and NVIDIA (VDA5050 fleet managers). Civilian examples only.
